items.title: After journo alleges sexual assault by Delhi ACP, those demanding FIR booked
items.summary: Around 20 people, some of them journalists and content creators, were detained by the Delhi Police on the morning of October 5 from outside the Parliament Street Police Station and taken to the Delhi Police Camp in Delhi Cantonment. They had been sitting outside the police station, protesting against the police for allegedly not registering an FIR against Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) Vivek Bhagat. Bhagat had been promoted as Additional DCP (Deputy Commissioner of Police) before withdrawing from the role “of his own volition” pending a “full enquiry” in the case, according to a government notification . A female journalist has alleged that Bhagat sexually harassed and assaulted her while she was covering the October 2 protest near Jantar Mantar. The police, however, have registered an FIR at the Parliament Street Police Station against 17 of the 20 people detained. Beauty, a friend of the complainant, said at a press conference on October 5, “The police have not filed an FIR on the sexual harassment and assault complaint but have filed an FIR against our people.” The 17 protesters were charged under Sections 223(a), 221, 132, 190 (unlawful assembly), 191(2) (rioting) and 3

items.title: A week of fear at SRFTI: Students demand safety after fresh violence
items.summary: “I returned from the hospital just a short while ago. A brick the size of my palm was thrown at me,” a student from the Satyajit Ray Film and Television Institute (SRFTI) in Kolkata told Newslaundry on October 4, the day of an incident in which bricks and stones were thrown from outside the college gate. She is one of two female students injured that day. She sustained a head injury that required stitches, while doctors advised the other to undergo a CT scan. The violence was the second flare-up at SRFTI in a week. On September 27, a scuffle broke out between members of the Akhil Bharatiya Grahak Panchayat (ABGP), an organisation linked to the RSS, who were attending an event they organised on campus, and SRFTI students protesting against it. A week later, on October 4, a rally associated with the Hindu Jagran Manch, a right-wing Hindu organisation, arrived at the college gate. Students allege that attempts were made to break down the gate and that stone and water bottles were hurled from outside. items.title: Delhi Riots: Delhi High Court rejects plea for action against politicians for hate speeches, probe into Jamia police violence
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Monday dismissed a batch of petitions seeking action against politicians for hate speech that allegedly led to the North-East Delhi riots of 2020. A Division Bench of Justices Vivek Chaudhary and Manoj Jain also dismissed a batch of petitions seeking an inquiry by a Special Investigation Team (SIT) into alleged police atrocities that took place in Jamia Millia Islamia in 2019 during a march against the Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA). A detailed copy of the judgement is awaited. Justices Vivek Chaudhary and Manoj Jain The order was passed in a batch of petitions seeking registration of FIRs against politicians for the speeches they delivered during the CAA and the National Register of Citizens (NRC) protests that allegedly instigated the riots in North East Delhi and ultimately led to the death of over 50 people. One of the petitions, filed by Shaik Mujtaba Farooq, sought registration of FIRs against Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leaders like Anurag Thakur, Kapil Mishra and Parvesh Sahib Singh Verma. items.title: Orissa High Court quashes pollution case against Tata Steel
items.summary: The Orissa High Court has quashed criminal proceedings against Tata Steel Limited over alleged air pollution violations committed by the erstwhile Bhushan Steel Limited (BSL), before Tata Steel took over the company through the insolvency resolution process [ Tata Steel Vs SPCB ]. Justice Sibo Sankar Mishra held that the protection under Section 32A of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC) prevented civil or criminal liability for acts attributable to the earlier management from being fastened on Tata Steel, after the resolution plan resulted in a change in management and control. “ Any civil or criminal liability arising from acts or omissions attributable to the erstwhile BSL cannot be fastened upon the present petitioner-company (Tata Steel) ,” the Court said. The Court consequently quashed the criminal proceedings against Tata Steel, while clarifying that it had expressed no opinion on the case against the remaining accused persons. items.title: Srinagar’s Smart City project is 98% done. But locals say it’s beautification without the basics
items.summary: In the second week of September, a cinema screen floated on the Dal. Srinagar was hosting the first International Film Festival of Jammu and Kashmir, with Chief Minister Omar Abdullah opening it against the Zabarwan hills. It was the city’s biggest international event since the G20 tourism meeting of 2023 and, like that one, mostly an argument made in pictures. Seven weeks earlier, on July 20, an hour of rain had put the same city under water. Lal Chowk, Polo View, Residency Road, the Boulevard, Khanyar, Sada Kadal, Nalamar, Bemina, Dalgate. Water got into the Civil Secretariat, of all places. By evening the valley’s papers had their verdict – so much for the Smart City – and the next day Abdullah called the Secretariat flooding a matter of shame. His cabinet, he said, had already ordered a third-party audit of the Srinagar Smart City project. What the audit will find is anyone’s guess. But what residents describe is fairly consistent. They point to roads raised over drains that still choke, a landfill that keeps growing, a lake that got new decks and cycle tracks but kept its sewage, and beautification in place of the basics.
